newsitem.title: UK: UK advertising body lobbies political parties.
newsitem.headline: UK advertising body lobbies political parties.

text.p: Britain's main advertising trade body said on Monday it was launching a big campaign at political party conferences in the next two weeks in defence of advertising.
The Advertising Association (AA) said in a statement it would hammer home a message to politicians from both sides of the political spectrum that advertising played a positive role in the economy.
AA starts its campaign at the Labour Party conference this week at the northern English seaside resort of Blackpool.
Next week it will be lobbying for support at the Conservative Party conference in Bournemouth.

The AA, which represents advertisers, ad agencies, media companies and related groups, said it would remind politicians that Britain's self-regulatory system for the advertising industry was working well.

"We aim to get the message across that advertising plays a significant role in the economy and enables business to compete," Jonathan Bullock, the AA's head of external affairs, said in the statement.
"We also want to show that the system of self-regulation in this country works and is constantly reviewed and refined," he said.
Britain's advertising industry has taken a leading role in defending the self-regulatory system that exists throughout much of Europe and in opposing moves to introduce statutory regulation.
